Lebanese journalist Christina Assi, who lost her right leg to an Israeli tank shell in southern Lebanon, accepted the CPJ International Press Freedom Award and warned that Israel has killed over 200 journalists in Gaza and Lebanon without ever being held accountable. She dedicated the award to her best friend, Reuters journalist Issam Abdallah, who was killed in the first blow of a double-tap strike on seven journalists in Alma al-Shaab on October 13, 2023. Investigations by AFP, Reuters, Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch and the UN peacekeeping force in Lebanon found the attack apparently deliberate and aimed at clearly identifiable members of the media.

Putin claims everything in Ukraine "collapsed" because "nationalists" took power after the collapse of the USSR: During the Soviet Union, I think there was a census in 1986 or so, and 51 or 52 million people lived on the territory of present-day Ukraine. It was one of the largest industrially developed territories in Europe. What happened after the collapse of the Soviet Union and Ukraine's independence? It lost its shipbuilding, aircraft manufacturing and rocket production industries. There was practically depopulation. A couple of decades later, the population was first estimated at 41 million, then 31 million, and now they say there are only about 20 million people left on Ukrainian territory. Everything collapsed. And not now, not in recent weeks under the retaliatory strikes of Russian missile forces. No, it collapsed on its own. Why? Because power in Ukraine was seized not by patriots of Ukraine, but by nationalists.

Putin on Ukraine: Those who live on the territory of present-day Ukraine must also understand that everything that is happening, and everyone who supports them in the current confrontation with Russia, is acting not in Ukraine's interests but in their own. The goal is to weaken everything, divide it, dismantle it into its component parts and subordinate it to their will. Understanding this, I believe all of us, including those living on the territory of present-day Ukraine, must strive for unity. Not necessarily within a single state. That is not what I am talking about at all. But unity in the broadest sense of the word.
